description:

This task removes the CURRENT data-layer plumbing. It does NOT build the show row itself — that is new UI that lands with the L8 show row (task #360, spec S23). All sites below were re-verified against the working tree on 2026-07-30 and their line numbers are current.

1. jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css (.viz-root:not([data-layer="2"]) .n-snap) — `.viz-root:not([data-layer="2"]) .n-snap { display: none; }`, the sole CSS rule gating snapshot-node visibility.

   - jfred/scripts/visual/layer2-checks.ts (LAYER),53,63,72,170 — the handoff cites only :18 and :53 (the `LAYER` const and one selector); re-verification found three MORE sites in the same 175-line file that also read `.dataset.layer` directly: :63 (`checkLayer1HidesSnapshots`), :72 (`openLayer2`'s waitFor), and :170 (the closing 2->1 round-trip check). All five must go together or this file's toggle-flow tests break.
   - jfred/scripts/visual/mockup-checks.ts (checkChrome) — `document.querySelector('[data-layer="2"]').title`.
6. jfred/docs/ui-component-glossary.md (§Layer 1 UI Component Glossary) ("top container `div.viz-root[data-layer="1"]`") and :28 (the "layer switcher" row naming `layer1-layer-toggle.ts` and `.layerbar button[data-layer]`) — update both to describe whatever replaces the toggle (or state plainly that the switcher is retired pending the show row, if that is the chosen interim).

title: Split the layer-2 fixture data out of viewer_api_layer1_fixture_data.ts
goal: - jfred/src/viewer_api_layer2_fixture_data.ts exists and exports FixtureSnapshot, SNAPSHOTS, and fixtureSnapshotPlacements
- jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_fixture_data.ts no longer defines or exports SNAPSHOTS, FixtureSnapshot, or fixtureSnapshotPlacements
- jfred/src/viewer_api_fixture_bulk.ts exists holding one parameterized bulk-generator loop plus the self-check, called exactly once
- Every prior import site of SNAPSHOTS/FixtureSnapshot/fixtureSnapshotPlacements builds against the new layer2 file
- Fixture-mode timeline shows the same bubble/instant counts before and after the split (verified by CDP page dump, not typecheck alone), and the full test suite plus typecheck pass
notInScope: - Extending the self-check to validate edit hunks (L3 hunk-validation) — owned by the not-yet-started L3 fixture-data task from spec S20
- Restructuring plans/layer2-mockup/fixture.js's file layout to mirror the new TS split — spec S19 keeps one mockup file for every layer; only the generated VALUES must stay equivalent
description:
Per plans/340-recon/DECISIONS.md ("Fixture data: one file per layer") and handoff plans/handoff-develop-20260730-1820.md step 6. Re-read the full 175-line jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_fixture_data.ts on 2026-07-30 to confirm the real structure — it is more entangled than "move SNAPSHOTS to a new file" suggests, so read this whole description before starting.

Current shape (verified line numbers):
- Lines 8-9: shared helpers `ms`/`basename`.
- Lines 11-20: fixture path constants + all five `Fixture*` interfaces (`FixtureTitleRange`, `FixtureCommit`, `FixtureDisk`, `FixtureSession`, `FixtureSnapshot`).
- Lines 23-71: hand-crafted `COMMITS`, `DISK`, `BRANCHES`, `SESSIONS` (layer 1 data).
- Lines 73-83: hand-crafted `SNAPSHOTS` (layer 2 data) — this is what DECISIONS.md says moves to the new file.
- Lines 86-89: `titleAt` (layer 1).
- Lines 91-131: ONE bulk-generation loop that builds 84 files' worth of `COMMITS`, `DISK`, and `SESSIONS` entries (layer 1) AND pushes into the SAME `SNAPSHOTS` array (layer 2, lines 121-122) in the SAME iteration, sharing the same `bulkSessions` map, `born`/`mtime` timestamps, and file-name generation. This is the loop DECISIONS.md means by "both layers' data comes from one loop" — it is not two adjacent loops, it is one loop with layer 1 and layer 2 pushes interleaved per-file.
- Lines 134-149: the import-time self-check, which currently validates only `SNAPSHOTS` against `DISK`/`SESSIONS` (born<=snapshot<=mtime, inside session window, on a title line) and throws on failure.
- Lines 152-174: `sessionIdFor`/`sessionFileFor` (layer-agnostic id/path helpers) and `fixtureSnapshotPlacements` (layer 2, builds the wire-shaped `SnapshotPlacement[]`).

Required split, per DECISIONS.md's exact wording ("the shared bulk generator and self-check move somewhere common"):
1. New jfred/src/viewer_api_layer2_fixture_data.ts gets: `FixtureSnapshot`, the crafted `SNAPSHOTS` array (lines 73-83), and `fixtureSnapshotPlacements` (lines 161-174).
2. jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_fixture_data.ts keeps: the path constants, `FixtureCommit`/`FixtureDisk`/`FixtureSession`, crafted `COMMITS`/`DISK`/`BRANCHES`/`SESSIONS`, `titleAt`, `sessionIdFor`/`sessionFileFor`.
3. A third, common module (name not prescribed by DECISIONS.md — follow the existing underscore convention, e.g. something under src/ that both layer files import) gets: the bulk generator loop's shared constants and helpers (`HOUR_MS`, `BULK_DIRS`, `BULK_EXTS`, `BULK_FILES`, `BULK_BORN0`, `iso`, `fakeHash`), the loop itself (parameterized so it can push into caller-supplied arrays rather than closing over module-level `COMMITS`/`DISK`/`SESSIONS`/`SNAPSHOTS`), and the self-check. Per section 3 of plans/coding-requirements.md ("DRY — extract to generic, parameterized helpers"), this must be a real parameterized function, not two copy-pasted loops.
4. The self-check itself must extend to edit hunks per spec S20 (specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md (§S20. Layer 3 — beacons and extracted Edit/Write nodes), "the import-time self-check extends to hunks") once L3's fixture file exists — this task does not need to add that logic yet (L3's fixture data is a separate, not-yet-started task per S20's Status line), but the common module's self-check should be written so a future `viewer_api_layer3_fixture_data.ts` can register its own validation into the same throw-on-load mechanism rather than duplicating it.
5. New layers beyond L2/L3 get their own `viewer_api_layer<N>_fixture_data.ts` (underscores, matching the existing family) as they're built — not part of this task, just the naming convention this split establishes.

HARD CONSTRAINT — keep the bulk loop intact. 84 of the 88 fixture bubbles come from this generator (verified: `BULK_FILES = 84`, plus the 4 hand-crafted sessions/paths = the fixture's ~88-bubble total cited throughout DECISIONS.md and the handoff). If the split breaks the loop's cross-population of COMMITS/DISK/SESSIONS/SNAPSHOTS, the fixture-mode mockup timeline renders near-empty. Verify bubble/instant counts are unchanged before and after the split (e.g. diff a page dump, or assert counts in a quick script) — do not rely on typecheck alone.

The static mockup twin, plans/layer2-mockup/fixture.js (verified: 174 lines, same COMMITS/DISK/SESSIONS/SNAPSHOTS/bulk-loop/self-check shape as the TS file, "ported wholesale" per its own header comment), does NOT get this same file-per-layer split. Spec S19 (specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md (§S19. Layer 2 View mockup — file-history snapshots)) explicitly decided one mockup file carries every layer ("no layer2-mockup.html copy" — a copy would fork the ruler/bubbles/minimap/etc into two files kept in step by hand). Splitting fixture.js's internal structure to mirror the new TS layout would contradict that decision. What DECISIONS.md's "kept in sync" requirement actually means here: the VALUES (which commits, disks, sessions, snapshots the bulk loop produces) must stay equivalent between fixture.js and the TS family after the split — verify by comparing generated content (e.g. bubble count, per-file snapshot counts), not by keeping the file layouts identical.

Check every import site of `SNAPSHOTS`/`FixtureSnapshot`/`fixtureSnapshotPlacements` from viewer_api_layer1_fixture_data.ts elsewhere in src/ and scripts/visual/ before moving them, and update those imports to the new layer2 file.

Depends on: None required to start. Loosely related to the (not-yet-created) L3 fixture-data task from spec S20, which will want the same common bulk-generator/self-check module this task creates — sequencing this first makes that task additive rather than another refactor.

title: Engine build-out: Layer 3 beacons and extracted Edit/Write nodes
goal: - npm run typecheck and full npm test pass with the new LayeredNodeKind member, buildEditDerivedNode, and Layer 3 fixture data in place
- Clicking an Edit/Write node in Layer 3 lazily replays it and shows a verified, derived, or reseeded confidence state, read from the engine response rather than computed in the browser

- A headless CDP visual-checks pass confirms fetch-once-with-progress, instant-toggle-after, the [e]/[R] checkmark, replay-opens-diff-and-flashes-JSONL, the {} raw-JSON button, an L3-free pair rendering byte-identical to Layer 2, and the mismatched-hunk fixture rendering derived not verified

- Defining the shared seven-state confidence vocabulary; that is task #376

description:
Spec item S20 in specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md (rewritten 2026-07-30) is the source of truth for WHAT to build; this task is the engine + webapp implementation behind the #343 mockup, not a restatement of it.

Engine must compute/expose, per S20's three stages: (1) Read tool results carrying full contents -> beacon; (2) Bash results carrying full contents (Bash(cat FILE) and friends) -> beacon, Bash stays excluded as a *change* source; (3) Edit/Write events applied onto the immediately preceding beacon -> provably verified beacons via structuredPatch base->target. Add buildEditDerivedNode beside buildNodeFromEvent (jfred/src/layered_load.ts (buildNodeFromEvent)) so an edit event emits the new L3 node kind instead of collapsing to a byteless preAnchorStub -- LayeredNodeKind (jfred/src/structures/vocabulary.ts (LayeredNodeKind)) currently has exactly five members (beacon, preAnchorStub, endState, presumedUserEdit, scriptRun) and none carries hunks. Replay stays lazy, triggered by node click: walk back to the nearest preceding beacon, replay any unpopulated intermediate nodes first (firstHunkMatchesBase / applyEdit, jfred/src/reconstruction_replay_edit.ts (applyEdit), both in-memory), and classify the result verified (matches the next beacon) or derived (does not). The one disk-touching step -- the BackupReader stale-base fallback (editBaseIsStale / staleEditSeedFor, jfred/src/reconstruction_reseed.ts (editBaseIsStale),127) -- is a per-HTTP-request read, copying the existing shape of readSnapshotFileContent -> createSidecarReader (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_snapshot.ts (readSnapshotFileContent)); a backup-seeded node renders as the 'reseeded' confidence state, one of the seven states settled in DECISIONS.md (never a bespoke marker). New NDJSON progress endpoint runs the existing extractFileEvents (jfred/src/reconstruction_extract.ts) over the configured sessions and joins each event's absolute target to a pair via relativizeToProjectFolder (jfred/src/layer1_snapshot_wire.ts (relativizeToProjectFolder)) -- the same join snapshots already use -- firing the first time the [3] preset OR its show-row checkbox becomes visible, per the visibility-triggers-computation rule in DECISIONS.md, scoped to nodes in the rendered viewport.

Webapp consumes, never re-derives: new wire field edits? on WirePairOf (jfred/webapp/layer1-wire.ts (WirePairOf), the snapshots? precedent), placed via listPairLadderInstants / listOrphanLadderInstants (jfred/webapp/layer1-wire.ts); a new appendEditNode + .n-edit class in jfred/webapp/layer1-widgets.ts; a describeNode branch in jfred/webapp/layer1-drawer.ts (describeNode) reading the existing data-session-id/data-session-file/data-line attribute contract (appendSnapshotNode, layer1-widgets.ts (appendSnapshotNode)) so JSONL Nav flashSession keeps working unchanged. Bubbles hold one lane per session (mvp-app-mockup.html precedent). The [{ }] raw-JSON button ports appendJsonRecordButton (views/timeline-render-row-cells.ts (appendJsonRecordButton)) / details-revision-cards.ts (buildRevisionActionsElement) rather than inventing a second idiom. The client never computes confidence state, never replays a patch itself, and never decides verified-vs-derived locally -- all three are read off the engine's response.

Fixture: new jfred/src/viewer_api_layer3_fixture_data.ts (one-file-per-layer convention). Every edit fixture carries a real structuredPatch ({oldStart, oldLines, newStart, newLines, lines[]}) because reconstruction_extract.ts (collectEditDetailFromRecord) builds no event without one. Edits go in both the 4 hand-written sessions and the bulk loop (84 of 88 bubbles are bulk-generated). At least one pair carries edits from two sessions; one edit's hunk deliberately does not match its base so 'derived' rendering is exercised, not just 'verified'.

Verify per S20's verify list: npm run typecheck, full npm test, and a headless CDP visual-checks pass (new file per S20's fixture-checks paragraph) confirming fetch-once-with-progress, instant-toggle-after, [e]/[R]checkmark rendering, replay-opens-diff-and-flashes-JSONL, the {} button, an L3-free pair rendering byte-identical to Layer 2, and the mismatched-hunk fixture showing derived not verified.

Depends on: #343 (L3 mockup) closed; no other layer's engine work blocks this one.

title: Engine build-out: Layer 5 branch rendering in per-file bubbles
goal: - Clicking a [3]-or-higher layer control triggers a session-scoped second fetch with a 'reconstructing branches' progress stage; nothing branch-related runs on page load
- A rewound branch renders as dimmed nodes (opacity .38) plus a dashed elbow connector, with no new rewind node kind added
- Ordinary parallel tool calls never render as fake abandoned branches (absorbParallelToolCallSiblings is honored on the branch-discovery path)
- npm run typecheck and npm test pass, including the new `branches?` wire field, per-node branch-role flag, and lane-aware groupTiedLadderNodes extension
notInScope: - Choosing the lane-rendering variant (per-session columns vs conversation-wide fork tree); that is decided by the L5 mockup, task #379
- Cross-session branch stitching (grafting a forked subagent's branch onto the parent tree before branch discovery runs); that is task #380
- Writing new branch-comparison or rewind-point logic; this task only composes the existing reconstruction_branch/trunk/fork/engine/worktree functions
description:
Recon: plans/340-recon/L5-branches.md. Critical finding: buildLayer1View reads NO JSONL and imports none of reconstruction_branch/graph/json (grep-verified zero hits) -- L5 needs a session-scoped second fetch, triggered on-demand, not a change to the initial view build.

Engine must expose: branch discovery is already parse-only and reusable as-is -- ConversationBranch = {tip, rewindPoint, isSurviving} (jfred/src/reconstruction_branch.ts (ConversationBranch)), built via findSurvivingHead -> findWorkingTreeOwner content-signature tiebreak, collectAbandonedHeads + findRewindPoint (jfred/src/reconstruction_trunk.ts (collectAbandonedHeads),:71), findStructuralRewoundBranches (jfred/src/reconstruction_fork.ts (findStructuralRewoundBranches)). Kept-vs-reverted (byte content, not a heuristic) is a composition that already exists: reconstructBranches(records, reader) (jfred/src/reconstruction_engine.ts (reconstructBranches)) returns surviving FileHistory[] plus per-rewound-branch RewoundBranchHistory with reconstructed revisions; findWorkingTreeOwner (jfred/src/reconstruction_worktree.ts (findWorkingTreeOwner)) decides which content owns the surviving tree by comparing rewind-moment snapshot CONTENT signatures; the branch-agnostic steps core (jfred/src/reconstruction_steps.ts) already models the conv-only-vs-code-rewind disk-survives-a-rewind case. L5's job is to compose these into per-node branch membership, NOT to write new comparison logic and NOT to re-derive rewind points -- MUST call absorbParallelToolCallSiblings (jfred/src/reconstruction_trunk_absorb.ts (absorbParallelToolCallSiblings)) via the existing branch-discovery path so ordinary parallel tool calls never render as fake abandoned branches.

Per DECISIONS.md: nothing branch-related runs on page load. Clicking a [3]-or-higher layer button/checkbox runs the normal page-load stages, then a ruler-resolving stage, then a stage labelled 'reconstructing branches' in the progress strip. There is NO rewind node -- a rewind renders as dimmed nodes (opacity .38, per mvp-app-mockup.html layer 8 precedent) plus a dashed elbow connector; do not add a rewind node kind. New wire field branches? on WirePairOf plus an isOrphaned/BranchRole-equivalent field per node (the old app's isOrphaned, reconstruction_json.ts (ConversationMessage.isOrphaned),59 / reconstruction_tool_calls.ts, is the closest existing precedent for the flag shape, though it lives in the classic pipeline). One ruler for the whole project -- forked lanes share the trunk's ticks, no local sub-axis.

Webapp consumes, never re-derives: the chosen lane-rendering variant from the L5 mockup (a separate task, per handoff step 1) -- port lane-run boundary logic (fork/end/rejoin) from the old app's flat-row computeGraphLaneRuns (webapp/views/timeline-sessions.ts (computeGraphLaneRuns)) / checkNodeIsAbandonedBranchTip (:79-89) re-derived for a bubble's vertical ladder, not copied verbatim. Bubbles widen to fit more than two lanes rather than stacking or hiding. The client never classifies a branch tip, never computes rewind points, and never decides kept-vs-reverted itself.

GATE, corrected per spec S25 (`specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md (§S25. Layer 5 — branches in bubbles (task #340 L5))`, written 2026-08-01, superseding this task's pre-S25 framing): blocked on the L5 visual mockup (#379) and the cross-session branch-stitching task (#380) landing. #357 predates the forked-track and lane-scope decisions in S25 and needs a re-read against it before being picked up — in particular, per-node branch membership is a NEW field (not `Verdict`, which is dropped before `FileEvent`s exist), and `groupTiedLadderNodes` (`jfred/webapp/layer1-tie-groups.ts`) needs a lane-aware extension since tie groups may now span a trunk lane and a forked lane at the same instant.

Depends on: #379 (L5 branch-rendering mockup) closed.

The lane-rendering variant and lane scope are decided by the L5 mockup #379, which must be closed before this task's webapp work can proceed.

title: Engine build-out: Layer 6 on-demand script execution replay
goal: - A new POST route takes a run/node id, calls executeRunOnce, checks the result against the unified beacon definition, and streams progress as NDJSON
- executeRunOnce tells 'original-failed' (the log's own is_error:true) apart from 'replay failed' or 'not replayed', confirmable by a test for each case
- getPostExecutionBeacon matches on file-history backup, full-file Read echo, Bash(cat) result, git commit, or snapshot, whichever is nearest after the run, not only backups
- A mismatch between replay output and the expected beacon renders as a distinct mismatch state instead of silently keeping the event unexplained
- A new GUI header button clears the sandbox memo and forces every layer to recompute, confirmable by clicking it and watching layers refetch
notInScope: - The execution-console popup and the node-states/mismatch mockup visuals are owned by #347 (done) and #381; this task consumes their signed-off design, it does not design it
- The shared WireConfidenceState type for the seven confidence states is owned by #376; this task consumes it
- Per-request consent gating beyond calling isImpureExecutionAllowed() as it exists today is not built here
description:
Recon: plans/340-recon/L6-script-results.md. This is the layer that actually spawns the sandbox; L4 only locates runs.

Engine must compute/expose: reuse executeRunOnce(run, records, reader, seedContent?) -> RunExecution{pre, post|undefined} (jfred/src/reconstruction_script_runs.ts (executeRunOnce)) and runScriptAgainstState (jfred/src/reconstruction_script_sandbox.ts (runScriptAgainstState), python3 only, execSync __script__.py, 5000ms timeout, cwd remapped into a temp dir so scripts can't escape). Wire is_error into executeRunOnce (~10-15 lines per the recon's cost re-check -- ScriptRun already carries toolUseId and records is already passed in; the toolUseId -> tool_result lookup idiom already exists twice: indexToolResultsByToolUseId, jfred/src/reconstruction_git_operations.ts (indexToolResultsByToolUseId), and collectRenameCandidatesFromToolResult, jfred/src/reconstruction_script_renames.ts (collectRenameCandidatesFromToolResult)) so an 'original-failed' run (the log's own is_error:true) is told apart from a 'replay failed' or 'not replayed' run -- three of the seven confidence states. Extend getPostExecutionBeacon (jfred/src/reconstruction_script_stage.ts (getPostExecutionBeacon), currently ONLY the file-history backup timeline via backupSeedWriteFor) to the ONE unified beacon definition settled in DECISIONS.md -- file-history backup, full-file Read echo, Bash(cat FILE) result, git commit, or snapshot, nearest AFTER the run -- so L6 never verifies against a different definition of 'beacon' than L3 does. A read-only script event yields beacon-level data itself (full contents reported) -- render it as a beacon, not an absent/empty node. A mismatch between replay output and the expected beacon becomes its own 'mismatch' node kind, not the engine's current silent fallback to keeping the original event unexplained (reconstruction_script_stage.ts, the caller today silently discards a verification failure). Add the live-working-tree read as a genuinely first-ever capability (process.cwd() appears nowhere in jfred/src/ today) used ONLY to CONFIRM a beaconless script-created file -- a match promotes to verified, a mismatch or missing file changes nothing and shows no marker, because a difference is not evidence the file wasn't touched since.

Execution scope and ordering (both settled, not open): only nodes in the rendered viewport execute, and only once per node, ever -- an off-screen node scrolled into view later is already done if its run already fired. Runs execute strictly in timeline order (no concurrency to design; each run depends on file state reconstructed by earlier points). Persistence reuses the existing sandbox memo disk file (configureSandboxMemoPersistence / flushSandboxMemoToDisk, reconstruction_script_sandbox.ts (configureSandboxMemoPersistence / flushSandboxMemoToDisk), SHA-256(script+cwd+sorted pre-state) key, batched every 64 spawns) plus a new button in the GUI top-row header that clears the memo and forces every layer to recompute from scratch. Consent reuses isImpureExecutionAllowed() (jfred/src/reconstruction_exec_gate.ts) as-is -- its own comment already flags per-request gating as a documented extension point, which this task exercises for the first time via an HTTP-triggered replay.

New route: run/node id -> executeRunOnce + stage match check -> streamNdjsonBuild progress framing (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_route.ts (streamNdjsonBuild), the existing ?progress=1 NDJSON precedent) -- 'scoped single-file GET with streamed progress' is a new composition of two existing pieces, not new machinery. New WireScriptResultOf wire type + node classes for verified/mismatch/original-failed/etc.

Webapp consumes, never re-derives: a genuinely new switcher interaction -- today the layer switcher is pure CSS and never refetches (layer1-layer-toggle.ts (wireLayerToggle),:23); L6 computing on switch, with progress, breaks that precedent deliberately and must fire from the global load bar plus the L6 execution console mockup UI (separate task). The client never spawns the sandbox itself, never compares replay output to a beacon itself, and never reads the live working tree itself.

GATE, corrected per spec S26 (`specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md (§S26. Layer 6 — script execution results (task #340 L6))`, written 2026-08-01, scope narrowed to real-execution-only since the visual mockup is now a separate item): blocked on the L6 node-states/mismatch mockup (#381) closing — the console popup mockup (#347) is done and unaffected. Real-execution behaviour follows S26 as written; no further spec pass is required (user decision 2026-09-08). The L4 dependency this task previously named is satisfied: `WireScriptRunOf`/`scriptRuns?` already exist on the wire, landed by closed task #356.

Depends on: #381 closed; L4 engine build-out landed so scriptRun instants exist to attach results to.

description:
Recon: plans/340-recon/L9-ruler-range-export.md. This is the ONLY layer that writes to git -- every existing git call in jfred/src/ today is read-only (grep-verified: zero git commit / git apply / git branch / checkout -b anywhere in src). L9 is not a layer either (adds no node kind); it is a mode you arm.

Model (settled, amends the older S16/S17 partition text): a growing prefix, not a partition. One marked range = one segment = one commit. The first commit's base is the commit chosen by a NEW ruler-base marker; each later commit's base is the current jfred-branch tip. You may stop at any time (no full-coverage requirement) but may NOT start in the middle -- chunks only extend the prefix, and a skipped stretch is absorbed into the NEXT commit with a message noting 'includes N unmarked changes', never omitted.

Engine must build: (1) generalize resolveRangeStepIndexes (jfred/webapp/layer1-diff-wash.ts (resolveRangeStepIndexes), today hard-coded to exactly 2 instants) to n cuts, each snapping PER FILE at-or-before to that file's nearest VERIFIED state -- unverified refused, never pulls future content backward, and v1 restricts markers to beacon nodes only (no derived node may carry a marker, so every jfred commit is provably a beacon, and any jfred commit counts as a beacon on the NEXT pass, resolving previously-unverified stretches as the branch extends). (2) A server-side per-file-per-segment diff loop + concatenation into one git-diff, reusing exportPatch's synthetic diff --git/---/+++ header-wrapper (jfred/webapp/layer1-diff-pane.ts (exportPatch), currently client-side, per-file, per-pane only) moved server-side and generalized across files. (3) A new route for apply-and-commit: git apply then git commit --date per segment, in commit order, author date = the mark's instant (always a real evidenced moment under the beacon-only rule), committer date = export wall clock, commit message carrying a footnote 'reconstructed by JFRED @ <real timestamp>' plus any per-file snap-variance note. Bytes are pinned at mark time, never re-read at commit time. (4) The jfred branch: created lazily on the first commit, forked from the ruler-base marker's commit (not an orphan root, not current HEAD), immutable base (delete the branch entirely to change it -- no amend, no reset, no force-push, append-only, so the app never rewrites history it did not just create), and hidden from the repo branch picker via a ONE-LINE filter in buildLayer1RefsView (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_refs.ts (buildLayer1RefsView), currently `git for-each-ref refs/heads` with no exclusion) so a reconstruction can never accidentally load against the synthetic branch. Also add the missing 'Branch picker' row to jfred/docs/ui-component-glossary.md, a documented gap the recon flagged.

Webapp consumes, never re-derives: arming state + mark placement lives in layer1-ruler-click.ts (makeRulerTickClickable) (today single-click only -- expand row / scroll to bubble -- no drag gesture exists yet, this task adds one). A NEW dedicated render strip beside the ruler shows jfred-branch commits with its own layout, hit-testing, and scroll sync -- nothing renders ON the ruler today, this is a genuinely new surface, not an extension of an existing one. v1 ships commit-only: no multi-file patch export UI; the existing per-file patch download stays exactly where it is (exportPatch, layer1-diff-pane.ts (exportPatch)). The client never computes a segment's diff itself and never issues git apply/commit itself -- both go through the new server route.

Spec item S24 is written; this task is blocked on the L9 mockup (#383) closing. Functionally depends on beacon nodes existing on the wire (at minimum L3, since v1 markers may only land on beacon nodes) before there is anything to mark.
